entry.description: The jit.lcd object is a wrapper for many QuickDraw commands.

messages.name: ascii
messages.digest: Write an ASCII character
messages.description: Writes the ASCII character specified by theargument at the current pen location using the current font and textmode, then moves the pen position to the right of that character. Numbers that exceed the 0-255 range are restricted to that range with a modulus operation.

messages.name: brgb
messages.digest: Set the background color
messages.description: Sets the current background color. All values should be in the range 0-255.

messages.name: clearpicts
messages.digest: Delete all of the object's named pictures.
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, deletes all of anobject's named pictures from memory so that they can no longer be drawn. To remove the images from theobject's display, the command should be followed by amessage.

messages.name: clipoval
messages.digest: Clip drawing commands to an oval
messages.description: Clips drawing commands to the oval specified byThe arguments are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

messages.name: clippoly
messages.digest: Clip drawing commands to the polygon
messages.description: Clips drawing commands to the polygon specified by the up to 254arguments. These integer pairs are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

messages.name: cliprect
messages.digest: Clip drawing commands to a specified rectanglar area
messages.description: Clips drawing commands to the rectangle specified by,,, andarguments. These integer arguments are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.

messages.name: cliproundrect
messages.digest: Clip drawing commands to a rounded rectangle
messages.description: Clips drawing commands to the rounded rectangle specified by,,,,, andarguments. These integer arguments are specified in pixels, relative to the top left corner of the viewing area.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, bottom:int, right:int, horizontal-roundness:int, vertical-roundness:int

messages.name: color
messages.digest: Set the current pen color
messages.description: Sets the current pen color to the value specified by theargument.

messages.name: deletepict
messages.digest: Delete a named picture
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, deletes the named the picture from memory so that it can no longer be drawn. To remove the image from theobject's display, the command should be followed by amessage.

messages.name: drawpict
messages.digest: Draw a named picture or matrix
messages.description: Draws the named picture or matrix. A destination rectangle into which the picture is scaled and drawn may optionally be specified by the,,, andinteger arguments. A source rectangle that specifies the area of the picture to use in the operation may also be optionally specified by the,,, andinteger arguments. The position of the destination and source rectangles are relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Unless otherwise specified, both rectangles are set to be the same size as the picture. All arguments are optional and default to zero. The current penmode will used as the transfer mode.
messages.argPattern: pict-name:symbol, x-offset:int, y-offset:int, width:int, height:int, src-x-offset:int, src-y-offset:int, src-width:int, src-height:int

messages.name: font
messages.digest: Set the current font name and size
messages.description: Sets the current font name and size. Fonts can be specified by either their ID number or name. Font size is specified in points.

messages.name: framearc
messages.digest: Paint the outline of an arc
messages.description: Paints the outline of an arc. The,,, andarguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of an oval across which the arc will be drawn, and theandarguments describe the position of the arc with respect to the oval. The location of the oval/arc is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. A color may also optionally be specified using a single number that selects a color from Max's color palette (similar to themessage), or by using three additional numbers that describe an RGB value (similar to themessage). The width of the line segment describing the arc is set using themessage to theobject.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, bottom:int, right:int, start-angle:int, arc-length:int

messages.name: frameoval
messages.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of an oval
messages.description: Draws the unfilled outline of an oval. The,,, andinteger arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of the oval. The location of the oval is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the border may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the border of the oval is set using themessage to theobject.

messages.name: framepoly
messages.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of a polygon arguments.
messages.description: Draws the unfilled outline of a polygon specified by up to 254 integerarguments. Each integer pair specifies a pixels relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. A polygon is closed by specifying an x/y pair having the same values as the first integer pair. The width of the border of the polygon is set using themessage to theobject.

messages.name: framerect
messages.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of a rectangle
messages.description: Draws the unfilled outline of a rectangle specified by the,,, andinteger arguments. The edge positions are specified as pixels relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the border may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the border of the rectangle is set using themessage to theobject.

messages.name: frameroundrect
messages.digest: Draw the unfilled outline of a rounded rectangle
messages.description: Draws the unfilled outline of a rounded rectangle. The,,, andinteger arguments describe the top and bottom extremities of the rectangle, and the Theandinteger arguments specify the amount of corner rounding in pixels. The location of the rounded rectangle is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the border may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the border of the rectangle is set using themessage to theobject.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, bottom:int, right:int, horizontal-roundness:int, vertical-roundness:int

messages.name: frgb
messages.digest: Set the current foreground color
messages.description: Sets the current foreground color. All arguments should be in the range 0-255.

messages.name: getpenloc
messages.digest: Get and output the current pen location
messages.description: Sends the x and y coordinates of the current pen location out the right outlet of the object as a list in the form. The numbers represent local coordinates relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. The first number is the number of pixels to the right of that corner, and the second number is the number of pixels down from that corner.

messages.name: getpixel
messages.digest: Get and output the color of a specified pixel
messages.description: Sends the color of the pixel specified by the x and y offset arguments and the coordinates out the object's right outlet as a list in the form. The three color values should be in the range 0-255. The pixel location is specified relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. If a pixel is out of range, themessage will output, whereandare the out of range location specified.

messages.name: line
messages.digest: Draw a line from the current pen position to a relative point.
messages.description: Draws a line from the current pen position to the relative point specified by two integerandarguments. The endpoint of the line becomes the new pen position. Positive values for theandarguments draw the line to the right or down, and negative arguments draw up or to the left.

messages.name: linesegment
messages.digest: Draw a line segment
messages.description: Draws a line segment. The,,, andarguments specify the start and end points of the line segment. The location of the start and end points is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the line segment may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color. The width of the line segment is set using themessage to theobject.

messages.name: lineto
messages.digest: Draw a line from the current pen position to a specified point
messages.description: Draws a line from the current pen position to the relative point specified by two integerandarguments. Positive values for theandarguments draw the line to the right or down, and negative arguments draw up or to the left.

messages.name: move
messages.digest: Move the pen position relative to its current location
messages.description: Moves the pen position relative to its current location. The new location is specified by the two integerandarguments. Positive values for theandarguments move the pen position to the right or down, and negative arguments move it up or to the left.

messages.name: moveto
messages.digest: Set a new pen position
messages.description: Sets the pen position at which the next graphic instruction will be drawn. The new location is specified by the two integerandarguments that are relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area.

messages.name: noclip
messages.digest: Remove clipping area that may be in place
messages.description: Removes any clipping area that may be in place.

messages.name: oprgb
messages.digest: Set the opcode color used in some of theobject's transfermodes
messages.description: Sets the current opcode color used in some of theobject's transfermodes, such as "blend". All arguments should be in the range 0-255.

messages.name: paintarc
messages.digest: Paint an arc
messages.description: Paints an arc. The,,, andinteger arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of an oval across which the arc will be drawn, and theandarguments describe the position of the arc with respect to the oval. The location of the oval/arc is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the arc may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, bottom:int, right:int, start-angle:int, arc-length:int

messages.name: paintoval
messages.digest: Paint an oval
messages.description: Paints an oval. The,,, andinteger arguments describe the top and bottom extremities in pixels of the oval. The location of the oval is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the oval may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.

messages.name: paintpoly
messages.digest: Paint a polygon
messages.description: Paints a polygon specified by up to 254 integerarguments. Each integer pair specifies a pixel relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. A polygon is closed by specifying an x/y pair having the same values as the first integer pair.

messages.name: paintrect
messages.digest: Paint a rectangle
messages.description: Paints a rectangle specified by the,,, andinteger arguments. The edge positions are specified as pixels relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the rectangle may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.

messages.name: paintroundrect
messages.digest: Paint a rounded rectangle
messages.description: Paints a rounded rectangle. The,,, andinteger arguments describe the top and bottom extremities of the rectangle, and the Theandinteger arguments specify the amount of corner rounding in pixels. The location of the rounded rectangle is relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area. Optional additional arguments to specify the color of the rectangle may also follow. If a single integer argument is used, it specifies a color from Max's color palette. Three integer arguments specify an RGB color.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, bottom:int, right:int, horizontal-roundness, vertical-roundness

messages.name: penmode
messages.digest: Set the transfer mode for drawing operations
messages.description: Sets the transfer mode for subsequent drawing operations. The transfer mode is set using an integer argument in the range 0-39. Since JUCE does not support pen modes, the only available penmode is 32 (Blend). All other penmodes are ignored.

messages.name: pensize
messages.digest: Set the pen size to be used in drawing operations
messages.description: Sets the pen size to be used in subsequent drawing operations. The pen size is set with two integer arguments, though the second argument is not supported due to differences in QuickDraw emulation.

messages.name: readpict
messages.digest: Read a picture file from disk into RAM.
messages.description: Reads a picture file specified by the symbolfrom disk into RAM. This named picture can then be drawn in lcd with theandmessages.

messages.name: reset
messages.digest: Erase the contents of the display area and reset the object to its default values
messages.description: Erases the contents of theobject's display area and resets the object to its default values. This message is equivalent to this series of messages to theobject:clearpensize 1penmode 0frgb 0 0 0 (black)brgb 255 255 255 (white)

messages.name: scrollrect
messages.digest: Move or "scroll" a rectangular area to a specified location
messages.description: Moves or "scrolls" a rectangle defined by the,,, andinteger arguments in the direction specified by theandinteger arguments. the first four arguments in the direction specified by the fifth and sixth ints within theobject's display area.
messages.argPattern: left:int, top:int, right:int, bottom:int, left:int, x-offset:int, y-offset:int

messages.name: setpixel
messages.digest: Set a pixel to a specified RGB value
messages.description: Sets the pixel located at the coordinates specified by theandcoordinates to the RGB value specified by the,, andarguments. The RGB values should be integers in the range 0-255. The pixel location is specified relative to the top left corner of theobject's display area.

messages.name: textface
messages.digest: Set the font style(s)
messages.description: Sets the font style(s) to be used when rendering text. Font styles may be specified individually with a single symbol argument, or as a list. Valid font styles are,,,,,,, and;

messages.name: textmode
messages.digest: Set the text rendering mode
messages.description: Sets the text rendering mode using an integer argument in the range 0-39. Supported textmodes are:0 = Copy1 = Or2 = Xor3 = Bic4 = NotCopy5 = NotOr6 = NotXor7 = NotBic32 = Blend33 = AddPin34 = AddOver35 = SubPin36 = Transparent37 = AddMax38 = SubOver39 = AddMinFor more information on the effects of each rendering mode, refer to the QuickDraw documentation in.

messages.name: tilepict
messages.digest: Fill a rectangle by tiling a picture
messages.description: Fills a rectangle by tiling a picture. The name of aobject can be used in place of the name of a PICT file, provided that the namedobject is a 4 plane char data matrix.
messages.argPattern: pict-name:symbol, dst-left:int, dst-top:int, dst-right:int, dst-bottom:int, src-left:int, src-top:int, src-right:int, src-bottom:int

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Write the text specified by theargument at the current pen location using the current font and textmode.
messages.description: Writes the text specified by theargument at the current pen location, using the current font and textmode.

messages.name: writepict
messages.digest: Write the current contents of theobject's display area to a PICT file.
messages.description: Writes the current contents of theobject's display area to a PICT file. If no filename argument is present, a Save As dialog will prompt you to choose a filename and location to write the PICT file.
